argument: chi2 = dp^T C^-1 dp with C = C_S + C_D assumes Cov(p_S, p_D) = 0. With a positive cross-survey covariance K the correct matrix is Var(dp) = C_S + C_D - K - K^T; if K + K^T is positive semidefinite this matrix is <= C_S + C_D in Loewner order (and still PD), so its inverse is >= (C_S + C_D)^-1 and chi2 can only increase. DESI DR2 estimates C ~ 0.57 for LRG2 vs eBOSS LRG. Hence the reported N_sigma is a lower bound with respect to survey overlap; the cross-survey K itself was not estimated here.
